correctness.rationale: The source Bernstein expansion immediately gives K_n≤S_n. If A_k is maximal, evaluating at λ=k/n gives K_n≥b_{n,k}S_n; the adjacent-ratio calculation places the minimum b_{n,k} at the central index. For k central coordinates equal to L and the rest zero, S_n is asymptotic to L^k/binomial(n,k), while the normalized optimized product converges uniformly to the kth Bernstein basis function, whose maximum is b_n. This proves optimality. The capped reciprocal ratio follows by the three threshold cases, and Stirling gives the stated asymptotic.

value.rationale: The motivating work advertises SymPol's pointwise advantage over optimized constant betting but leaves its possible magnitude unspecified. The exact best finite-sample factor answers that natural calibration question completely and shows the gain can grow on, but not exceed, the square-root scale.
residual_risks: An approximation-theory source may record an equivalent sharp Bernstein-coefficient envelope under different terminology.

final_claim: For every nonnegative n-vector, optimized constant betting K_n and SymPol S_n satisfy K_n≤S_n≤K_n/b_n, where b_n is the central binomial point mass; 1/b_n is the optimal uniform factor, is attained in the supremum by sparse diverging vectors, gives the same sharp capped-p-value ratio, and is asymptotic to sqrt(pi n/2).
limitations: Worst-case deterministic envelope only; typical power or confidence-interval improvement may be much smaller.
Does not compare SymPol against every e-to-p merger.
